questionsReviewed.independentReasoning: Solving y=(x-1)/(2-x) gives x=(2y+1)/(y+1). The identity f(x)+1=1/(2-x) excludes -1, and every other real y gives an allowed preimage.
The antiderivative 4 sin^2(x) follows by u=sin(x), and gives 4 at the upper endpoint and 0 at the lower endpoint.
Viete gives -2 and -3. Substituting (1,3) and f′(1)=0 gives 6a+b=3, 7a+b=0, hence a=-3,b=21.
Normalization gives q=0.3; the expectation is 2.3-p, so p=0.2. Every resulting probability lies in [0,1].
Domain x>-1 is essential. Changing to base 2 gives x+2=2(x+1)^2; roots 0,-3/2 leave only x=0.
S8-S3 is the five terms u4 through u8, with mean u1+5d; its vanishing implies u1=-5d. Then u6=0, including d=0.
Both sides are positive in the stated quadrant, so squaring is reversible. sin(2x)=1/2 with 0<2x<180 degrees gives exactly 15 and 75 degrees.
Expanding the dot product yields 3|a|^2+8 a.b-3|b|^2. As a.b=0 and norms are nonnegative, zero is equivalent to equal norms, in both directions.

At y=2 the ellipse has x=0 and a horizontal tangent. A line with normal (cos theta,sin theta) supports this ellipse at distance sqrt(cos^2 theta+4sin^2 theta); equality to sqrt(2) gives sin^2 theta=1/3.
All integrals use the bounded continuous density. Integral dx/(1+x^2)=arctan x, x dx/(1+x^2)=ln(1+x^2)/2, and x^2/(1+x^2)=1-1/(1+x^2). The CDF is strictly increasing on [0,1].
Exponential positivity makes the derivative positive on all reals, so f is injective. Writing f=2-3/(e^(2x)+1) yields limits -1 and 2. The inverse input 1 lies in the range.
A tangent through the origin satisfies f(t)=t f′(t), hence t=5. For the rectangle S′=e^(a/5)(1-a/5), positive before 5 and negative after, proving the global maximum on [0,10).
